newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close 2.36 pct up as bonds welcomed.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close 2.36 pct up as bonds welcomed.

text.p: Foreigners bought large capitalised stocks on Tuesday as sentiment improved after the Thai cabinet approved an issue of 100 billion baht zero-coupon bonds to aid the ailing property sector, brokers said.

"Foreigners gained more confidence in the market after the cabinet approved earlier in the day the issue of zero-coupon bonds to help the property sector. The announcement sparked buying power," said Sonyos Kulvichien of Securities One.
The SET index gained 16.63 points, or 2.36 percent, to close at 719.95, just below the day's high of 719.95, on 5.3 billion baht turnover.
The SET-50 index gained 1.58 points to 53.67.
Gainers led decliners 240 to 82 while 67 issues were unchanged.
"The cabinet's decision to issue the zero-coupon bonds has also made foreign investors believe that the bonds would help boost liquidity for financial institutions," said Songyos.

Central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said earlier that proceeds from the bond issue would be used for refinancing troubled property projects and for easing liquidity problems of their creditor banks and finance companies.

All the major sectors, except the building and furnishing materials sector, gained on Tuesday. The banking sector gained most in terms of value, rising 4.56 percent. The finance sector rose 3.58 percent while the property sector advanced 1.30 percent and the building sector slipped 0.49 percent.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list, gaining 10 baht to 187, National Finance and Securities rose 2.25 to 36.50 and United Communication Industry shed one to 160.
Support is seen by some brokers at around 705 on Wednesday and resistance at 730. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
